Extract the First Structural Match and Named Captures

rex_match.Rd

Extract the first match and its named capture groups from each glycan.

Usage

rex_match(glycans, pattern)

Arguments

glycans

A character vector of glycan expressions in any format supported by glyparse::auto_parse(), a glyrepr_structure vector, or one glyrepr-compatible igraph. Character inputs may mix formats; malformed structures throw an error.

pattern

A character vector of patterns or one rex_compile() object. Inputs recycle only from length one. Missing glycans or patterns propagate.

Value

A character matrix with one row per input, a match column, and columns for named captures. No match or missing input produces a missing row; unmatched captures are NA. Fragments are canonical glyrepr IUPAC strings. Vectorized patterns must have identical capture names.

Details

A match is identified by its complete set of graph nodes and the node set assigned to each named capture. Repeated search routes to the same identity are collapsed; different capture assignments remain distinct, even when their extracted strings or location rows are identical.

At the same actual starting residue (the first consumed node), the first successful trace wins over later traces with identical capture assignments whose node sets contain it or are contained in it. Incomparable branch choices are retained. Search order follows pattern alternatives and greedy (longer first) or lazy (shorter first) repetition. Among these selected traces, strict subsets are removed only when capture assignments agree. Thus different captured sites or captured repeat lengths are preserved, including for lazy repeats. An unmatched capture differs from an empty one.

Results are ordered by decreasing residue count, then minimum node ID, then lexicographically by sorted node IDs and capture assignments to break ties. This order is deterministic for a given input graph; renumbering can change the order, but IDs always refer to that input graph. Matches may overlap. Counts therefore need not equal text-regex counts. These rules replace the earlier one-match-per-minimum-node and capture-blind subset filtering. Only connected rooted trees are supported; floating topology or floating substituents are rejected explicitly. See rex_compile() for syntax.

See also

Other glycan queries: rex_count(), rex_detect(), rex_extract(), rex_extract_all(), rex_locate(), rex_locate_all(), rex_match_all(), rex_subset(), rex_which()

Examples

x <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc", "Fuc(a1-3)GlcNAc", NA)
rex_match(x, "(?<terminal>Gal)-GlcNAc")
#>      match                 terminal 
#> [1,] "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(?1-" "Gal(b1-"
#> [2,] NA                    NA       
#> [3,] NA                    NA
